heuristics: H1: the mixed add/square class walk on N = (r-1)/12 classes with r_a = 1024 and S = 458 square slots behaves as a random map with collision rate V = 0.799413681 (sum of squared branch probabilities of the actual partition).

H2: every walk checks 2-cycles every step and cycles of length 3 to 64 against a per-walk anchor refreshed every 64 of its own steps; a detection escapes by squaring the least-key state. The 2-cycle branch is exercised by exact replica checks; the longer-cycle branch is mirrored in the replica and fired once in 2^27 production steps.

H3: c2 = 0.1445 and kappa = 0.4902 are Callgrind measurements at S = 458 from interval counts on two seeds (agreeing to 0.01%); the per-step operation counts come from uninstrumented runs of 2^26 steps per seed.
H4: a detected cycle wastes at most 127 main steps; the measured event rate upper bound 4.6044e-05 per step gives a wasted fraction 0.005848, charged in the budget.
limitations: H1 is extrapolated from toy groups with N up to 2^17 and r_a = 32; production N is about 2^251 and r_a = 1024.
No production-size execution of the walk to a collision; the replica checks full dumps and distinguished-point records at 512 and 4096 rounds, and samples of production states.
Storage of about 2^73 bytes is not realisable; memory is reported, not scored.
The reference unit is priced by the organizer rule (1 unit); the measured reference count is 22,998 against C = 20,000.
